newsitem.title: USA: Westinghouse acquiring TNN, CMT networks from Gaylord.
newsitem.headline: Westinghouse acquiring TNN, CMT networks from Gaylord.

text.p: Westinghouse Electric Corp., essentially completing its transition to a broadcasting company, said Monday it agreed to buy two country music cable television networks from Gaylord Entertainment Co. for $1.5 billion in stock.

Westinghouse, which acquired CBS Inc. in late 1995 and is spinning off its industrial businesses, said it had a definitive agreement to acquire the domestic and overseas operations of The Nashville Network (TNN) and the North American operations of Country Music Television (CMT) network.
Pittsburgh-based Westinghouse, which is also acquiring Infinity Broadcasting Corp. to add to its CBS and Group W radio networks, said the deal includes about $50 million of working capital.

Shareholders of Gaylord, based in Nashville, will receive $1.55 billion in Westinghouse common stock in the transaction, which is intended to be tax-free to Gaylord and its shareholders. Gaylord also owns the Grand Ole Opry, the Opryland theme park and Opryland Hotel in Nashville.
Jack Bergen, Westinghouse spokesman, said the transaction should close early in the third quarter, before Westinghouse splits its media and industrial operations into separate companies.
The number of shares to be issued by Westinghouse will depend on the average price of its stock during a trading period just prior to the closing of the transaction.
Westinghouse Chairman Michael Jordan said in a statement the acquisition will have a positive impact on the company's earnings.

"Having built a preeminent radio group with the Infinity acquisition and now establishing a strong position in cable, we complete the major actions on the investment priorities we established at the time of the CBS acquisition," he said.
Analysts said Westinghouse paid a fair price for the cable networks based on their current value and the acquisition will add about $108 million in cash flow.
Ed Hatch at UBS Securities said the transaction will give Westinghouse leverage if it wants to expand in sports programming. TNN broadcasts popular sports events, including NASCAR stock car racing.

"It gives Westinghouse added entertainment distribution and increases their ability to buy more sports programming," he said. "If they want to make a bid for the NFL, they have another distribution channel through which to do that."
Analysts also said the transaction will let Gaylord focus on increasing its presence in the hotel and convention business.

Gaylord on Monday reported that net income for the fourth quarter rose 22 percent to $27.4 million, or 28 cents a share, from $22.4 million, or 23 cents a share, while revenues expanded by 11 percent to $194.0 million from $174.7 million.

For all of 1996 Gaylord said its net income grew 21 percent to $131.2 million, or $1.34 a share, from $108.4 million, or $1.11 a share, as revenues rose 6 percent to $747.2 million from $707.5 million.
Gaylord said revenues from its two cable networks increased 20 percent to $84.3 million in the quarter and by 17 percent to $331.8 million for the year.
Westinghouse and Gaylord have had a partnership since 1982, with Gaylord providing content of TNN and CMT and Group W Satellite Communications providing advertising sales and marketing.
Edward Gaylord, chairman of Gaylord, said the cable stations would be best served as part of a media company.
"For some time we have seen consolidation in the cable broadcasting industry. Our judgment is that further growth of TNN and CMT can best be served as part of a larger media company," he said.
CBS already owns eight country music radio stations, including WUSN-FM in Chicago, the nation's most popular country music station.

Currently reaching over 70 million households in the United States and Canada, TNN is the second-largest North American cable network and the eighth-largest in the United States. CMT has 38 million subscribers in the United States.

Also included in the merger are CMT Canada, a joint venture with Shaw Cable of Canada, several cable production companies, and NASCAR Thunder, a chain of retail stores themed on NASCAR stock car racing.
Westinghouse shares lost 25 cents to $17.50 on the New York Stock Exchange, while Gaylord fell $2.50 to $22.875, also on the NYSE.
